ann_79.original: Linear backbone (identity_0 sums the 39 direct input->output edges). Largest weights per sd: voiceMailPlan -0.71, numberCustomerServiceCalls +0.49, state:2 -0.33 (cancelled by state2_switch), state:46 -0.24, state:11 -0.22, numberVmailMessages +0.18, totalNightCharge +0.16, state:47 +0.15, totalIntlCharge +0.135 and totalIntlMinutes +0.125 (identical columns after z-scoring, so the net intl usage slope is +0.26/sd split across both), totalDayCalls +0.11, plus ~25 small state/area offsets. Evidence: closed form exact (linear); on train the backbone alone (hidden units at their means) gives AUC 0.692; together with linearised hidden units it gives 0.840 (refit L2 LR: 0.843). Day minutes and eve charge/minutes have no direct edge: their effect is entirely in the usage hinges. Direct state edges are the network's per-state offsets: largest net effects state:46 -1.70 (80 rows, empirical log-odds offset -0.83), state:11 -1.68 (73, -1.22), state:4 +1.28 (41, +0.84), state:47 +1.16 (72, +0.95), state:26 +0.94 (75, +0.53); several exceed the empirical offset, i.e. rare-category overfitting.
ann_79.proposed: A mostly linear backbone: customer-service calls and voice-mail messages slightly raise the chance of leaving, a voice-mail plan slightly lowers it, and California and Washington raise it to about 8% to 9% on the training data only.

ann_80.original: Customer-service-calls threshold. 1044 = relu(0.722 csc - 0.006 eveCalls - 0.718), output weight +1.65. csc z-levels: 0..9 calls = -1.20 + 0.766k, so the unit is 0 for 0-2 calls, +0.12 logit at 3 calls, +1.03 at 4, then +0.92 per extra call (eveCalls term negligible). Combined with the direct +0.37 logit/call slope this makes the CS-call effect convex: observed churn rate 0.11 for 0-3 calls, 0.44 at 4, 0.57 at 5, 0.68 at 6. Evidence: closed form max err 0.001; heatmap(train, 4000 rows) shows dependence on csc only. Linearising this unit alone costs 0.0067 train AUC; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model adds +0.022.
ann_80.proposed: A customer-service step: calls slightly add to the chance of leaving from 3 calls upwards (about 3% to 7% at 4 calls).

ann_81.original: Serial chain 3453 -> 2636 -> 4722. 3453 = relu(0.504 csc - 0.206) (on from 3 calls), 2636 = relu(0.25 csc + 0.221*3453 - 0.107 state:8 - 1.45) fires on only 0.4% of train rows (7+ calls), 4722 = relu(0.85*2636 + 0.494) is always on, so the chain is a constant +0.36 logit (0.727*0.494) plus a tiny extra slope at 7-9 calls (+0.02 to +0.36). Hypothesis confirmed: near-inert. Sensitivity (train) <0.001 for all entries; linearising or restoring it changes AUC by <0.0001. state:8 has zero effect on train (2636 never on for state:8 rows).
ann_81.proposed: A near-constant chain with a slight Delaware adjustment, on the training data only.

ann_82.original: 252 = relu(0.215 csc - 0.373 dayMinutes - 0.123), output weight +0.96. Active on 37% of rows: low day usage, amplified by CS calls. For customers with >=4 CS calls it adds +0.85 logit in the lowest day-minutes quintile, +0.53, +0.35, +0.13, +0.06 in the next quintiles; for <=3 calls only +0.35 at the lowest quintile. This encodes the data's CS x usage interaction: among >=4-call customers churn is 0.97 / 0.63 / 0.41 / 0.09 / 0.24 by day-minutes quintile. Evidence: closed form err 0.0007; heatmap on train. Restoring alone onto the linearised model: +0.015 AUC; linearising alone: -0.0012.
ann_82.proposed: Low daytime usage: fewer daytime minutes slightly raise the chance of leaving, below about 149 minutes.

ann_83.original: 1683 = relu(0.439 dayMinutes - 0.072 area408 - 0.715), output weight +1.45. Fires only for dayMinutes z > ~1.6 (5.6% of rows), up to +1.04 logit at the top. A second, steeper heavy-day-usage hinge; area408 shifts the knee negligibly. Evidence: closed form err 0.0013; heatmap on train. Small marginal value because day_eve_usage covers the same region: restore alone +0.004 AUC, linearise alone -0.0001.
ann_83.proposed: A very heavy daytime-usage step acting on 223 customers, raising a typical such customer's chance of leaving from about 66% to 71%, a little less in area code 408, on the training data only.

ann_84.original: 3151 = relu(0.515 day + 0.508 relu(0.921 day - 0.075) + 0.585 relu(0.93 day + 1.18 eveCharge + 0.189) - 0.384 csc - 0.957), output weight +1.73. A convex function of day minutes and evening charge (eveCharge == eveMinutes after z-scoring; the network uses only the charge column), switched down by CS calls. Mean logit added by day-minutes bin (q0-20,20-40,40-60,60-80,80-90,90-100) x eve tercile: 0 below the median; 0.03/0.24/1.29 in 60-80%; 0.40/1.19/2.34 in 80-90%; 1.96/3.02/4.43 in the top decile, matching churn rates up to 0.71 for top-day x top-eve. With >=4 CS calls the term is much smaller (e.g. 0.32 vs 1.34 in the 80-90% bin), so high-usage and many-calls risks do not stack. Evidence: closed form err 0.009; sensitivity (train) spread over day copies (0.17,0.16,0.14), eveCharge 0.21, csc 0.12. This is the single largest nonlinear source: linearising it alone drops train AUC 0.899 -> 0.874; restoring it alone onto the linearised model raises 0.840 -> 0.889.
ann_84.proposed: Heavy daytime and evening usage: daytime minutes add to the chance of leaving above about 210 minutes (about 3% to 39%), far more when the evening charge is above 17.12 US dollars, while customer-service calls lower it for the customers it acts on.

ann_85.original: 4939 = relu(0.65 intlPlan + 0.14 relu(0.99 state:6 + 0.387) - 0.699), output weight +1.86; 8417 is always on (affine in state:6). Effectively: +2.50 logit for international-plan customers, 0 otherwise, plus a state:6 bump: +0.22 for state:6 without the plan and +4.34 (i.e. +1.84 extra) for the 7 train rows with state:6 AND intl plan (5/7 churned vs 42% of intl-plan customers overall). Linear fit R^2 0.993, so it is essentially a one-hot offset; linearising or restoring changes AUC by 0.0001. The state:6 x intlPlan term is a rare-category interaction fitted to 7 rows. No intl-plan x intl-minutes interaction is present (intl usage enters only linearly).
ann_85.proposed: An international-plan switch: the plan raises the chance of leaving from about 3% to 24%, and to about 62% in Connecticut.

summary.text: For a typical customer (one in West Virginia with area code 415, an account length of 100, no international or voice-mail plan, one customer-service call and median usage such as 180 daytime minutes), the model predicts about a 3% chance that the customer leaves, and an international plan clearly raises that to about 24%.

Through one part of the model, daytime minutes clearly add to it only once they rise above about 210 minutes: for the typical customer, going from 0 to 271 minutes moves it from about 3% to about 39%.

That part makes daytime minutes count far more when the evening charge is above 17.12 US dollars: going from 112 to 249 minutes clearly raises the chance from about 3% to about 32%, against about 3% to about 9% otherwise.
An international plan clearly raises it even more for customers in Connecticut: from about 3% to about 62%, against about 3% to about 24% elsewhere.

In the usage part, customer-service calls clearly lower it: for the typical customer that part acts on (one in Alabama with about 231 daytime minutes), going from 0 to 3 calls moves it from about 13% to about 3%.

Being in California or Washington rather than one of the states the model does not single out raises it to about 8% to 9% (on the training data only), and the model ignores account length, the daytime charge and international calls.

parts.name: churn_logit
parts.original_hypothesis: P(churn) = sigmoid(-1.318 + linear_backbone + 1.65 csc_threshold + 0.727 csc_extreme_chain + 0.962 low_day_csc + 1.45 high_day_hinge + 1.73 day_eve_usage + 1.86 intl_plan_gate - 1.26 state2_switch - 0.024 state25_switch - 0.058 state32_night - 0.243 state22_38_switch). Purely additive in the logit: no child gates another; interactions live inside children (CS calls x day usage in low_day_csc and day_eve_usage). 24 inputs (accountLength, areaCode:415, totalDayCharge, totalIntlCalls, 20 states) are unconnected and have zero effect. Note totalDayCharge is identical to totalDayMinutes after z-scoring; the network uses only the minutes column; for evening it uses only the charge column, and for intl/night it uses both (split slope). Evidence (train, 4000 rows): AUC 0.899; refit L2 logistic regression 0.843; all children linearised 0.840; backbone only 0.692. The ~0.059 AUC above linear comes from day_eve_usage (+0.049 restored alone), csc_threshold (+0.022) and low_day_csc (+0.015), sub-additive (all usage+CSC hinges together +0.059); state units and the intl gate add ~0. SHAP top: dayMinutes 0.073, CS calls 0.057, intlPlan 0.056, voiceMailPlan 0.038, eveCharge 0.031. Zeroing all state one-hots costs 0.0075 train AUC (0.899 -> 0.891).
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: day_eve_usage
parts.original_hypothesis: 3151 = relu(0.515 day + 0.508 relu(0.921 day - 0.075) + 0.585 relu(0.93 day + 1.18 eveCharge + 0.189) - 0.384 csc - 0.957), output weight +1.73. A convex function of day minutes and evening charge (eveCharge == eveMinutes after z-scoring; the network uses only the charge column), switched down by CS calls. Mean logit added by day-minutes bin (q0-20,20-40,40-60,60-80,80-90,90-100) x eve tercile: 0 below the median; 0.03/0.24/1.29 in 60-80%; 0.40/1.19/2.34 in 80-90%; 1.96/3.02/4.43 in the top decile, matching churn rates up to 0.71 for top-day x top-eve. With >=4 CS calls the term is much smaller (e.g. 0.32 vs 1.34 in the 80-90% bin), so high-usage and many-calls risks do not stack. Evidence: closed form err 0.009; sensitivity (train) spread over day copies (0.17,0.16,0.14), eveCharge 0.21, csc 0.12. This is the single largest nonlinear source: linearising it alone drops train AUC 0.899 -> 0.874; restoring it alone onto the linearised model raises 0.840 -> 0.889.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: linear_backbone
parts.original_hypothesis: Linear backbone (identity_0 sums the 39 direct input->output edges). Largest weights per sd: voiceMailPlan -0.71, numberCustomerServiceCalls +0.49, state:2 -0.33 (cancelled by state2_switch), state:46 -0.24, state:11 -0.22, numberVmailMessages +0.18, totalNightCharge +0.16, state:47 +0.15, totalIntlCharge +0.135 and totalIntlMinutes +0.125 (identical columns after z-scoring, so the net intl usage slope is +0.26/sd split across both), totalDayCalls +0.11, plus ~25 small state/area offsets. Evidence: closed form exact (linear); on train the backbone alone (hidden units at their means) gives AUC 0.692; together with linearised hidden units it gives 0.840 (refit L2 LR: 0.843). Day minutes and eve charge/minutes have no direct edge: their effect is entirely in the usage hinges. Direct state edges are the network's per-state offsets: largest net effects state:46 -1.70 (80 rows, empirical log-odds offset -0.83), state:11 -1.68 (73, -1.22), state:4 +1.28 (41, +0.84), state:47 +1.16 (72, +0.95), state:26 +0.94 (75, +0.53); several exceed the empirical offset, i.e. rare-category overfitting.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: intl_plan_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: 4939 = relu(0.65 intlPlan + 0.14 relu(0.99 state:6 + 0.387) - 0.699), output weight +1.86; 8417 is always on (affine in state:6). Effectively: +2.50 logit for international-plan customers, 0 otherwise, plus a state:6 bump: +0.22 for state:6 without the plan and +4.34 (i.e. +1.84 extra) for the 7 train rows with state:6 AND intl plan (5/7 churned vs 42% of intl-plan customers overall). Linear fit R^2 0.993, so it is essentially a one-hot offset; linearising or restoring changes AUC by 0.0001. The state:6 x intlPlan term is a rare-category interaction fitted to 7 rows. No intl-plan x intl-minutes interaction is present (intl usage enters only linearly).

parts.name: csc_threshold
parts.original_hypothesis: Customer-service-calls threshold. 1044 = relu(0.722 csc - 0.006 eveCalls - 0.718), output weight +1.65. csc z-levels: 0..9 calls = -1.20 + 0.766k, so the unit is 0 for 0-2 calls, +0.12 logit at 3 calls, +1.03 at 4, then +0.92 per extra call (eveCalls term negligible). Combined with the direct +0.37 logit/call slope this makes the CS-call effect convex: observed churn rate 0.11 for 0-3 calls, 0.44 at 4, 0.57 at 5, 0.68 at 6. Evidence: closed form max err 0.001; heatmap(train, 4000 rows) shows dependence on csc only. Linearising this unit alone costs 0.0067 train AUC; restoring it alone onto the fully linearised model adds +0.022.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: state2_switch
parts.original_hypothesis: 2808 = relu(1.76 - 2.21 state:2), output weight -1.26: 2.07 for every non-state:2 row (-2.60 logit, absorbed into the bias) and 0 for state:2, i.e. +2.60 logit for state:2. It nearly cancels the direct state:2 edge (-0.33/sd = -2.41 between levels), so the net state:2 offset is only +0.19 (78 rows, empirical log-odds offset +0.32). A cancelling pair, not a real effect. Linear fit exact; AUC unchanged by linearisation.

parts.name: low_day_csc
parts.original_hypothesis: 252 = relu(0.215 csc - 0.373 dayMinutes - 0.123), output weight +0.96. Active on 37% of rows: low day usage, amplified by CS calls. For customers with >=4 CS calls it adds +0.85 logit in the lowest day-minutes quintile, +0.53, +0.35, +0.13, +0.06 in the next quintiles; for <=3 calls only +0.35 at the lowest quintile. This encodes the data's CS x usage interaction: among >=4-call customers churn is 0.97 / 0.63 / 0.41 / 0.09 / 0.24 by day-minutes quintile. Evidence: closed form err 0.0007; heatmap on train. Restoring alone onto the linearised model: +0.015 AUC; linearising alone: -0.0012.
variables: number of calls to customer service

parts.name: high_day_hinge
parts.original_hypothesis: 1683 = relu(0.439 dayMinutes - 0.072 area408 - 0.715), output weight +1.45. Fires only for dayMinutes z > ~1.6 (5.6% of rows), up to +1.04 logit at the top. A second, steeper heavy-day-usage hinge; area408 shifts the knee negligibly. Evidence: closed form err 0.0013; heatmap on train. Small marginal value because day_eve_usage covers the same region: restore alone +0.004 AUC, linearise alone -0.0001.

parts.name: state32_night
parts.original_hypothesis: 16043 = relu(nightCalls + 0.924) feeds 699 = relu(0.838 state:32 + 0.189*16043 - 1.11), which fires only for the 72 state:32 rows; output weight -0.058 gives -0.29 to -0.33 logit depending on night calls. The direct state:32 edge is +0.33, so the net state:32 offset is about +0.03 (empirical -0.10). Another cancelling pair; negligible.

parts.name: state22_38_switch
parts.original_hypothesis: 5143 = relu(1.03 - 0.103 state:22 - 0.409 state:38), output weight -0.24: off for state:38 (+0.27 logit) and reduced for state:22 (+0.18 logit). state:38 offset has the wrong sign versus the data (56 rows, churn 0.071, empirical log-odds offset -0.66). Linear fit exact; AUC unchanged.

parts.name: state25_switch
parts.original_hypothesis: 12245 = relu(state:25 - 1.94), on only for the 77 state:25 rows (value 5.2), output weight -0.024: -0.12 logit, partly cancelled by the direct state:25 edge (+0.17); net +0.05. Negligible.

parts.name: csc_extreme_chain
parts.original_hypothesis: Serial chain 3453 -> 2636 -> 4722. 3453 = relu(0.504 csc - 0.206) (on from 3 calls), 2636 = relu(0.25 csc + 0.221*3453 - 0.107 state:8 - 1.45) fires on only 0.4% of train rows (7+ calls), 4722 = relu(0.85*2636 + 0.494) is always on, so the chain is a constant +0.36 logit (0.727*0.494) plus a tiny extra slope at 7-9 calls (+0.02 to +0.36). Hypothesis confirmed: near-inert. Sensitivity (train) <0.001 for all entries; linearising or restoring it changes AUC by <0.0001. state:8 has zero effect on train (2636 never on for state:8 rows).
variables: number of calls to customer service

reference_patient.definition: the typical patient: the median training patient for every number and the most common training category for every category (not a real patient)

confidence_rules.clearly: a meaningful change in predicted risk for a typical patient (at least 5% points), the test split agrees (same sign, and its bootstrap interval over test patients excludes no benefit), and every group has at least 20 training patients
confidence_rules.consistently across patients: the claim holds for at least 90% of training patients (range across patients); this is not a significance statement
confidence_rules.on the training data only: the test split disagrees (opposite sign, or no benefit on test patients) or is unclear (its interval includes no benefit), or no test check is available
confidence_rules.slightly: the change in predicted risk for a typical patient is below 5% points
confidence_rules.the model has little data on this: a compared group has fewer than 20 training patients

settings.effect_scale: log-odds (output pre-activation) for verification; predicted risk for the typical patient for wording

The model gives a clearly higher predicted chance that a customer leaves if the customer has an international plan than if the customer has no international plan, and even more so if the customer is in Connecticut: for a typical customer, going from no international plan to an international plan moves the predicted chance that a customer leaves from about 3% to about 62% if the customer is in Connecticut, and from about 3% to about 24% if state is something other than Connecticut.

Through one part of the model, total daytime minutes only clearly adds to the predicted chance that a customer leaves once it rises above about 210 minutes: for a typical such customer, going from 0 minutes to 271 minutes moves it from about 3% to about 39%.
The model ignores account length, total daytime charge and total international calls.
